probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L6 isolated perfused rat liver records show morphine hepatic clearance of 26.0–26.8 mL/min, approaching the 30 mL/min perfusate flow, indicating near-flow-limited hepatic extraction.

Human and rat hepatocyte/microsomal intrinsic-clearance records show substantial morphine glucuronidation (human hepatocyte CLint 17–28 µL/min/10^6 cells; UGT2B7-mediated M3G/M6G formation), consistent with extensive first-pass metabolism.

Naloxone retains the free phenolic 3-OH and morphinan ether scaffold of morphine, and its 6-keto and N-allyl substituents add carbonyl-reduction and N-dealkylation soft spots; the near-flow-limited first-pass clearance documented for morphine therefore transfers to naloxone and supports F < 20%.

The prior high-F evidence from codeine (80.5%) and ethylmorphine (28–74%) is less transferable because their 3-O-alkyl groups block the major phenolic glucuronidation site, whereas naloxone has a free 3-phenol like morphine; morphine's own F is only 29.2 ± 7.2%, just above the threshold.
Diacetylmorphine-derived morphine F estimates of 57–61% reflect morphine after prodrug conversion and do not address naloxone's own first-pass metabolism.
